title: Fuselage — Fwd Cargo Door Surround — Survey of Frame Feet Before Protection Standard Change

ata.title: Fuselage Section 13 — Forward — Door Surround Structure

abstract: Borescope and eddy current survey of the frame feet at the forward cargo door surround, done before the protection standard change so that the extent of existing material loss is known before the joint is opened.

sections.planning_reason: Aircraft delivered before the production cut-in of the chromate-free protection and drainage standard carry a fully sealed frame foot that traps condensate. Experience on the first twelve retrofits showed that on aircraft above 45 000 flight hours the material loss behind the foot can already be beyond blend-out limits, and finding that out with the joint open and the aircraft in a check slot is expensive. This Service Bulletin establishes the condition first, so that the operator can order the correct renewal parts and plan the right amount of time before committing the aircraft.
sections.description: A borescope survey of the frame foot to skin interface is made through the existing systems penetrations, followed by an eddy current survey from the accessible side over the full length of each foot between the door sill and the stringer 46 escape route. The result is recorded on a standard form and reported to Aeralis so that the population statistics stay current. Nothing is disturbed and no part is replaced. Aircraft found within blend-out limits proceed directly to the protection standard change; aircraft outside them require an engineering assessment first.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Get access to the forward cargo compartment and remove the lower shell lining panels in zones 111 and 121. Do the removal steps of AMM-S-53-21-13-000-001-A up to and including the removal of the sill closing panel, and stop there. Clean the frame foot area and remove any loose corrosion product by hand. Do a borescope survey of the foot to skin interface at each frame station and record the position and extent of any indication. Do an eddy current survey of the accessible face of each foot with a 2 MHz probe and record the maximum indicated material loss. Compare the recorded loss against the limits in the accomplishment instructions. Complete the survey form and send it to Aeralis. Install the sill closing panel and the lining panels. No functional test is required.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to SOLANO-30 and SOLANO-34 aircraft that have not been brought to the chromate-free protection and drainage standard. Aircraft delivered from MSN S00992 onward are already at that standard in production and are not affected by this Service Bulletin.
sections.material_note: No kit is required. Consumables are limited to cleaning agent and inspection developer. The eddy current probe and the borescope are standard workshop equipment. There is no mass change because nothing is installed or removed.

type_data.compliance_time: Before the accomplishment of Service Bulletin SLN-53-1012, and in any case at the next scheduled C-check for aircraft above 45 000 flight hours.
